records.title: Normalizing Unmanned Aircraft Systems Beyond Visual Line of Sight Operations (Part 108 NPRM)

badge.text: Proposed; no final rule on record

records.text: The long-awaited FAA/TSA 'Part 108' proposed rule laid out performance-based regulations to enable routine low-altitude BVLOS drone operations without visual observers, plus third-party UAS Traffic Management services. Issued under EO 14307's mandate, it is the foundational rulemaking for normalizing commercial drone flight in U.S. airspace.
kv: The August 7, 2025 FAA/TSA NPRM proposed a scalable BVLOS framework: Part 108 permits or operating certificates, aircraft airworthiness acceptance, and Part 146 oversight of automated data-service providers. Statutory authority includes the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 as well as the policy direction in EO 14307. The January 28, 2026 reopening was a limited further consultation, not final adoption.

records.title: Part 108 BVLOS — Denial of Extension of Comment Period

badge.text: Proposed; no final rule on record

records.text: The FAA and TSA denied requests to extend the Part 108 BVLOS comment period, citing EO 14307's 240-day final-rule deadline and the extraordinary measures needed to meet it. The denial signals the administration's push to fast-track the drone rule rather than slow the rulemaking.
kv: Part 108, BVLOS, comment period, EO 14307, fast-track

The September 29, 2025 procedural notice denied two requests for more comment time and retained the October 6 deadline. It cited statutory and executive scheduling pressures. The original “fast-track” reading describes that decision’s policy context; it is not evidence that the final rule arrived. FAA subsequently reopened limited electronic-conspicuity questions in January 2026.

records.title: Part 108 BVLOS — Reopening of Comment Period

badge.text: Proposed; no final rule on record

records.text: The FAA reopened the Part 108 BVLOS comment period to take additional input on electronic conspicuity and right-of-way provisions. The reopening shows the agency refining the highest-friction technical pieces of the drone rule as it moves toward a final rule.
kv: Part 108, BVLOS, electronic conspicuity, right-of-way, comment period

The January 28, 2026 notice reopened comments for fourteen days on alternative electronic conspicuity. FAA described seven questions following January 6 listening sessions and a January 15 docket memorandum; over half of roughly 3,100 earlier comments concerned right-of-way. Earlier comments remained in the record. This is evidence of a specific unresolved design issue and additional consultation, not an adopted right-of-way entitlement.

records.title: Designation — Restrict the Operation of Unmanned Aircraft in Close Proximity to a Fixed Site Facility
records.text: The FAA proposed to implement Section 2209, creating a process for operators of critical fixed-site facilities to request unmanned-aircraft flight restrictions on safety or security grounds. It is the security-side complement to BVLOS expansion — the airspace-protection layer the broader drone-integration push depends on.
kv: Section 2209, fixed-site facility, flight restriction, UAS security, airspace

The May 6, 2026 NPRM proposed Part 74 procedures for standard and special unmanned-aircraft restrictions around eligible fixed sites, implementing statutory §2209 and EO 14305. A restriction would be a legal airspace designation, not permission for a proprietor to jam, seize or destroy a drone. The June 30 extension moved comments from July 6 to August 5, 2026. This remains a proposal on the reviewed instruments, not proof that a particular site received protection.

records.title: Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program — Establishment and Request for Proposals
records.text: The FAA formally established the eVTOL/AAM Integration Pilot Program directed by EO 14307, pairing state, local, tribal, and territorial governments with private eVTOL operators to develop frameworks for safe air-taxi operations. The notice opened a request for proposals to select participating projects.
kv: eIPP, eVTOL, advanced air mobility, air taxi, pilot program

The September 16, 2025 notice established eIPP and solicited government/private partnerships for eVTOL and other advanced aircraft, including fixed-wing and short-takeoff designs. Participation agreements did not transfer FAA airspace authority. FAA’s August 6 and August 18, 2026 releases report eight projects across 26 states selected in March and completed hybrid-electric demonstrations in Utah and the PA/NJ corridor. These later receipts move the program beyond solicitation while preserving aircraft and service limits.
